testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Replace a tire.
Remove the alternator belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you need to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve stops air tanks from building up too much pressure. It is set to open at 150 psi.

questions.question: The ABS light stays on after starting the engine if:

options.text: The ABS is working properly.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS is not engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS light should turn on when you start the engine, then turn off. If it stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance you travel between deciding to brake and actually pressing the brake pedal.
The distance you travel between seeing a hazard appear and noticing it.
The distance you travel between seeing a hazard and deciding to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you travel between deciding to brake and actually pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has three parts: perception distance, reaction distance, and braking distance. Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels from when you decide to brake until you actually hit the brakes.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert while driving?

options.text: Stay fit and healthy.
Keep the cab warm.
Eat heavy foods.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay fit and healthy.
questions.explanation: Heavy foods and warm cabs make drivers sleepy. Exercising and eating healthy help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: Which vehicle requires the driver to have a CDL?

options.text: A military vehicle.
A school bus.
An emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school bus.
questions.explanation: A CDL is not required for military vehicles, emergency vehicles, or farm equipment. A school bus driver must have a CDL.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others.
Operating an unsafe vehicle.
Operating a vehicle that has not been inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others.
questions.explanation: Road rage means operating a vehicle with the intent to harm others or physically assault another driver or their vehicle. Aggressive driving is different—it is selfish, bold, or pushy driving.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
Push the clutch out when the engine is close to idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is close to idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.
questions.explanation: To stop smoothly, apply steady pressure to the brake pedal. If you have a manual transmission, push the clutch in when the engine is close to idle.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.

options.text: Air pressure.
Electricity.
Gasoline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure.
questions.explanation: Air pressure keeps spring brakes in place while you drive. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: If you don't drain air tanks, what could happen?

options.text: Water in the tanks could freeze and cause brake failure.
The brakes become soft and spongy.
Too much air builds up in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water in the tanks could freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems need regular draining to remove water and oil. If water is left in the tanks, it can freeze when it's cold outside and cause your brakes to fail.

questions.question: When are you most likely to experience strong winds?

options.text: When you exit a tunnel.
When you enter a tunnel.
When you drive on road shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you exit a tunnel.
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. The biggest wind problems happen when you drive out of a tunnel.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
After you finish driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you begin driving. Your sitting position may change, so your mirrors may need adjustment each day.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the storage tanks.
It fills the vehicle's tires.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks in an air brake system. The governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: What should you do when driving long distances?

options.text: Take rest breaks.
Drive as fast as you can.
Drive through the night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours to avoid getting too tired. Driving at night or when you would normally be asleep increases your risk of fatigue.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, what must your vehicle do?

options.text: Shift to the right.
Start in third gear.
Not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. Rolling backward could hit the vehicle behind you.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?

options.text: 2 psi per minute
4 psi per minute
6 psi per minute

questions.correctAnswerText: 6 psi per minute
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: How many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position during testing exercises?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during testing exercises. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can only look once. For all other exercises, you can look up to two times.

questions.question: What happens if a law enforcement officer asks you to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test and you refuse?

options.text: You can refuse without any penalty.
You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL.
questions.explanation: Most states have Implied Consent Laws. By driving on public roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if a police officer asks. If you refuse, you will lose your driving privileges. Check the laws in every state where you drive.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire that is missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you do not drive faster than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Check that your tires and rims are in good condition before driving your commercial truck.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:

options.text: Much safer.
Just as safe.
More dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on a phone. Texting distracts your mind and also takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Temporarily release the spring brakes.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the correct control will release the spring brakes for a short time. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before driving:

options.text: No part of your vehicle should be visible in any mirror.
Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: When properly adjusted, your mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. Seeing your own vehicle in the mirrors helps you judge where other objects are.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of tie-down equipment?

options.text: Ropes
Straps
Velcro

questions.correctAnswerText: Velcro
questions.explanation: You must use the correct number of tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Examples of tie-down equipment include ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is encouraged because:

options.text: The driver will have the best possible view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can offer assistance on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will have the best possible view.
questions.explanation: When backing, turn the vehicle toward the driver's left side. This gives the driver the best view of the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, it is important that you:

options.text: Plan how you would handle dangerous situations.
Enjoy the scenery.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how you would handle dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: While driving, constantly watch the road for hazards. Think about what you will do if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: A steering wheel should be:

options.text: Held with one hand while the other hand rests.
Held with both hands for a strong grip.
Released if the vehicle is approaching a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: Held with both hands for a strong grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, you must:

options.text: Park your vehicle uphill.
Park your vehicle downhill.
Leave the engine running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?

options.text: Every three hours.
Every day.
Every other week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every day.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: Your brakes fail while driving downhill. What is the best way to stop?

options.text: Steer onto an escape ramp.
Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Let rumble strips slow your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer onto an escape ramp.
questions.explanation: Use an escape ramp to stop your vehicle. If no ramp is available, drive onto an open field or side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: What does an alcohol evaporator in an air brake system do?

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator adds alcohol to the air brake system. This helps prevent ice from forming in the system.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you check in the fifth wheel gap?

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a tractor-trailer connection, look into the fifth wheel gap and make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light might be:

options.text: An impaired driver.
A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know the rules of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver.
questions.explanation: Stopping at a green light is a sign that a driver may be impaired. Impaired drivers have slowed reactions due to alcohol, drugs, sleepiness, or illness.

questions.question: What should you do if suspension parts are broken?

options.text: Repair them immediately.
Repair them, but not immediately.
Cannot be identified.

questions.correctAnswerText: Repair them immediately.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be repaired right away.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between the tires and road
How fast tires rotate
The time it takes to activate the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between the tires and road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. You need good traction to brake and steer safely.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems within about 45 seconds.

questions.question: How do you sober up after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Exercise.
Wait.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time will help your body remove alcohol. Your liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers and coffee do not speed this up.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air, what does this mean?

options.text: The compressor needs more air.
The air pressure has become too high.
The brakes are fully operational.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure has become too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and needs to be fixed by a mechanic.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, what happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
You get an extra point taken off your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the test.

questions.question: Why should you drain the air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced.
Because water collects in the tanks from compressed air.
To allow pressure to change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because water collects in the tanks from compressed air.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and oil that build up in the air tanks and can damage the brake system. You should drain the tanks to remove these materials. On tanks with a manual drain valve, drain them at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Get upset.
Accept it and drive at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you realize you will be late, take a deep breath and accept the situation. Continue driving safely.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, the hoses should be:

options.text: Checked for leaks.
Securely connected to the battery.
Carrying fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: While driving, you:

options.text: Can send text messages.
Can read text messages but cannot send them.
Cannot hold a phone to make voice calls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot hold a phone to make voice calls.
questions.explanation: You cannot hold a phone to make voice calls while driving. You also cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest speed to drive is:

options.text: Slower than surrounding traffic.
The same speed as surrounding traffic.
Faster than surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel at the same speed in the same direction, they cannot collide.

questions.question: An application pressure gauge shows:

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps drivers know if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Back up straight, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When alley docking, you should first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, first pass the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley. Your vehicle must be parked straight and within the space boundaries.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Be done the same way every time.
Be done differently every time.
Not always include all items to check.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes it less likely you will forget to check something.
